notes: Five exterior-renovation jobs, before+after, 14 frames in mixed light (2 low-res text-thread screenshots), the Ridge Road pair diverging on limestone (warm before/cool after) with a pale pergola against a pale overcast sky, a lost maker's-stamp mark surviving only on a screen-res plate and a painted truck door, an A6 press card with a near-square photo well and one continuous copy flow, and an 11-row export hiding one duplicate and one withheld job.

LAYOUT SPEC for the retired printer's press file (render as a flat, print-ready A6 PORTRAIT press PDF, trim 105 x 148 mm, no bleed, all fonts embedded/subset).

--- PAGE STRUCTURE (one card per job) ---
Top: a placed PHOTOGRAPH well, NEAR-SQUARE, approx 89 x 84 mm, centered with a 8 mm margin left/right/top. [In the printer's own file a square job photo happened to fill this well exactly, so the well was drawn near-square and the card never advertised it.]
Beneath the well, a small engraved GABLE & GROVE gable emblem + wordmark, approx 22 mm wide, centered.
Beneath the mark: FOUR copy lines, authored as ONE CONTINUOUS TEXT FLOW inside a single text frame (they render visually as four lines but are one story, no separate frames):
  {{job_name}}  — display serif, ~13 pt, e.g. "Marble Dale"
  {{location}}  — humanist sans, ~8.5 pt, e.g. "Marbledale, Connecticut"
  {{scope}}     — humanist sans, ~8.5 pt, e.g. "Full exterior renovation. Cedar siding, rebuilt entry, stone steps."
  {{season}}    — humanist sans small caps, ~7.5 pt, e.g. "SUMMER 2025"
Footer: hairline rule + small caps "BUILT TO LAST, SOLD TWICE", ~6.5 pt, centered.

--- STATIC CONTENT AS IT WENT TO PRESS LAST SEASON (placeholder job, to be replaced by the merge) ---
Job name: Sabin Road
Location: Cornwall, Connecticut
Scope: Front walk and steps rebuilt in granite, regraded approach, planting.
Season: AUTUMN 2024

Colours: text Honest Black #17140F on Bone #EDE9E1 stock; the season line prints in Grove Green #1E3A2F. Photograph reproduced at 300 dpi within the near-square well.

NOTE FOR THE RENDERER: keep the four copy lines a single continuous story (not four boxes) and keep the photograph well NEAR-SQUARE, so a wide after-crop bound to this frame is centre-cropped and can lose the finished feature at its edges.

assets.content:
GABLE & GROVE — A PAGE FROM MICHAEL (owner). How we want to look, and what we do not.

The yard signs are printed in our deep green. The sign shop has it as Grove Green, #1E3A2F. Everything green on our stuff is that green, nothing brighter.

The mark. The fellow who drew it for us is gone, packed up his shop two years back, and never sent the file. What we have is the picture he emailed us once and a photo of it painted on my own truck door. That mark means the house peak and the trees, it is a maker's stamp, not a sale sign. It has to work from a shirt to a yard sign, and on a yard sign it sits on the green.

The money and the people. We run between forty-five and a hundred and twenty thousand dollars a project. Our people are fifty to sixty-five, they own old houses and they are not in a hurry. They are getting two or three bids and they buy on trust, not on the lowest number. We sell everything twice, once on the site and once out of a quote pack on somebody's kitchen table.

When I say I don't want it looking HGTV, I mean the afters cannot look like a supermarket flyer or a paint-can ad. No fake blue skies, no cranked-up green grass, no glow. Cool, calm, real stone, honest blacks, one photograph doing the work. The befores stay exactly as honest as they came off the phone, because the before is the whole proof. If a before looks improved, we are lying, and these people can smell it.

One thing on permissions. The CHAPIN ROAD homeowners were very good to us but they have asked us NOT to publish anything from their job — no photos in the quote pack, on the site, on the showroom board, anywhere. Everything else last season is cleared to show. Please leave Chapin Road out and just tell me you did.

— M.
assets.defect_engineered: carries the CONSENT withholding for Chapin Road (the fact absent from projects.csv), plus the Grove Green hex, the price band, the audience and the HGTV/honesty standard; itself clean
